title: Nvidia’s board says it won’t bring Jensen Huang back, hours after he offered to return
summary: Nvidia is not looking to take back its founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, chairman Harvey C. Jones said on the company’s earnings call on Tuesday, TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2026. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said. Earlier Tuesday, Huang had posted on X that if the board decided his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America, he “would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang resigned last week following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. The scandal has spurred an independent board investigation and an SEC probe into Nvidia. Interim CEO Colette Kress, also the chipmaker’s CFO, is leading the company while the board considers internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement.

title: Nvidia stops selling H200 chips in China and creates a board committee for national security
summary: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending its participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on advanced chip sales to the country, TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2026. The H200 deal, brokered by Jensen Huang and President Donald Trump, required the chips to be shipped through the U.S. so the government could collect a 25% tariff. Even before the decision, China had largely refused to accept delivery of the chips. The same day, Nvidia created a standing board committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risks. Jefferies forecast that new U.S. rules on remote chip access might trim $44 billion to $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year, but Kress said the backlog of demand for chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on top-line revenue.

title: Study finds leading AI models can be tricked into picking military targets by being told it’s a game
summary: AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek and other labs could be easily tricked into identifying targets for military strikes, including civilians and surrendering soldiers, according to a new report from AI evaluation startup Vals, TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2026. Researchers used simulated scenarios and a mix of generated and real imagery from Ukraine and Iran to see whether models would mark targets in drone and satellite images. When models refused, researchers jailbroke them by claiming the battlefield scenarios were part of a game. None of the requests were blocked by a safety classifier, refusals were uncommon, and Anthropic’s models performed the worst. Anthropic said the outcomes were not acceptable and that additional safeguards would be in place soon. OpenAI said it prohibits such uses and is developing additional safeguards for its public models against misuse involving drones and drone software.

title: Waymo pulls its robotaxis off freeways nationwide after a California DMV order
summary: Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the company’s operations following several safety incidents, TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2026. The DMV issued the restrictions on November 11 after three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame and another incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280. The department said Waymo’s driverless freeway operations “pose an imminent hazard to public safety” due to recurring incursions into active construction zones. Waymo has complied and is keeping its robotaxis off freeways in all of its markets, including those outside California, while it evaluates performance. The company said its service continues on surface streets, “serving over half a million trips each week.” Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025 and has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.

title: S&P 500 falls for a fourth straight day as Nasdaq futures rise on Nvidia’s earnings beat
summary: U.S. stock futures were mixed Wednesday morning after the S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight day, CNBC reported in live markets coverage that began on November 17, 2026. Nasdaq-100 futures were up 0.6%, S&P 500 futures added 0.2% and Dow futures fell 55 points, or 0.1%. On Tuesday, the Dow dropped 1.6%, the S&P 500 slipped 1% to its lowest close since July 29, and the Nasdaq Composite shed 0.7% after touching its lowest level since April during the day. Nvidia was almost 3% higher in premarket trade after beating estimates, and neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius rose 4.4% and 6% in extended trading. Traders are awaiting housing data and minutes from the Fed’s October meeting, while Anthropic’s IPO shares are expected to price above the current $70 to $78 range, sources told CNBC’s David Faber.

title: Nvidia beats with $115.8 billion in revenue and raises its outlook, sending shares up after hours
summary: Nvidia delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday despite the turmoil following Jensen Huang’s departure, TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2026. Interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago and above the company’s $108 billion guidance for the third quarter of fiscal 2027. She projected fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, and said Nvidia now expects fiscal 2028 revenue to grow about 75% year over year, up from 70%. Nvidia spent $28.1 billion buying back its own shares during the quarter and has $227.3 billion remaining for repurchases. The stock is down about 10% since Huang’s departure, but shares rose about 4% in after-hours trading on the results. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual,” Kress said.

title: Anthropic’s 825 million-share IPO heads for a Thursday debut as chip stocks slide
summary: Anthropic is marketing 825 million shares at an expected $70 to $78 each ahead of its November 19, 2026 debut on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, Chip Dispatch reported on November 18, 2026. The listing arrives as a widely held semiconductor ETF fell 14.0% over the month through the November 17 close, while a Nasdaq-100 tracking fund lost 7.5%. Anthropic’s S-1 reports first-half 2026 revenue of $16.286 billion, up from $1.163 billion a year earlier, with an operating loss that narrowed to $693 million from $2.135 billion. Its net loss of $80.748 billion mostly reflects a $72.388 billion accounting adjustment tied to convertible notes and other private-funding instruments. A founder entity’s single Class F share will carry 50.1% of total voting power, and the company’s Long-Term Benefit Trust will elect four of seven directors.

title: Oracle hovers near its $116 stock-sale price as Nvidia signals a demand surge
summary: Oracle closed at $115.00 on Tuesday, 65% below its September 2025 peak of $328.33 and one dollar under the $116 at which it sold $10 billion of stock two weeks ago, Chip Dispatch reported on November 18, 2026. Nvidia’s results after the bell lifted Oracle about 2.1% in premarket trading Wednesday, to $117.46 at 6:50 a.m. Eastern. Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said “with demand far exceeding supply, we expect our performance to remain strong” and listed Oracle’s cloud, OCI, among partners already on Nvidia’s new Vera CPU. Oracle buys those chips with borrowed money and new shares, and its remaining performance obligations stood at $664 billion on August 31. About 45% of that backlog is tied to an OpenAI contract worth about $300 billion over five years, and Oracle plans $90 billion to $95 billion of capital spending this fiscal year.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting frontier prices by 20%
summary: OpenAI released two models from its GPT-6.2 line on November 17, 2026: Astra, a frontier model for complex tasks, and Sol for everyday routines, mlllm.io reported. Astra is aimed at code, document processing, 3D and cybersecurity, and its rate of $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens is 20% cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. The cost of the cache was cut by 60%, and its lifespan is no longer limited. Sol kept its previous rate of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Both models are already available in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. mlllm.io called the release an incremental iteration focused on economics rather than new capabilities, noting that key quality figures rely on vendor benchmarks.

title: Australia’s sovereign AI model Agentaus 1 opens to the public
summary: Canberra-based Trellis Data has opened access to its sovereign language model Agentaus 1, which has 220 billion parameters, mlllm.io reported on November 18, 2026. According to the company, the model scores 84.4% on MMLU-Pro and ranks 43rd globally among foundation models. It runs exclusively on Australian infrastructure, and the creators say user data does not leave the country and is never used for training. Pricing includes Standard subscriptions at 24 AUD and Professional at 107 AUD per month, plus API access at 1.70 AUD per million input tokens and 6.70 AUD per million output tokens. Organizations can also get an air-gapped deployment without an internet connection. The only disclosed technical detail is that the model is about 50% larger than Trellis Data’s previous one.

title: Higurashi AI opens Haru-4B, a speech model that listens while it talks
summary: Higurashi AI has released Haru-4B, an open speech-to-speech foundation model built to listen while it talks, Open Model Weights reported on November 17, 2026. It is designed for interruptions, backchannels and overlapping conversation, which can sound unnatural in a rigid chain of transcription, language generation and speech synthesis. A Qwen3.5-4B-based language model processes the user’s audio, the model’s audio and generated text in continuous frames at 7.5 Hz, roughly one frame every 133 milliseconds. Higurashi says it trained on more than 40 million hours of real speech across more than 160 languages. The weights are released under Apache-2.0 with PyTorch, MLX and vLLM-Omni inference paths. Open Model Weights notes that Haru is a pretrained base, not an instruction-tuned assistant, and that its reported 65-millisecond Mac latency excludes audio framing.

title: DeepMind spinout Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to take AI-designed drugs to clinical trials
summary: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery company spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 billion in a Series C round as it seeks to take its drug candidates to clinical trials, TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2026. The round was co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with new investor Andreessen Horowitz also participating. Isomorphic builds an AI drug-design engine on DeepMind’s AlphaFold work and says its program has yielded “positive preclinical results” in oncology and immunology. It has struck deals with Eli Lilly, Novartis and Johnson & Johnson. The funding follows a $2.1 billion Series B in May and will go toward the design engine and new types of medicine. The company did not disclose its valuation.

title: Three engineers and an AI agent built a 55-pound-payload cargo drone in six days
summary: Startup Normal published a breakdown on November 16, 2026, of Project Heavy Lift, in which three engineers working with its Zeus AI agent designed, ordered parts for and assembled a cargo drone in six days, mlllm.io reported on November 17. The project ran from October 31 to November 7, and the drone, with a payload capacity of up to 55 pounds, completed its first flights under FAA Part 107 rules and delivered cargo from November 5 to 7. From a single specification, the agent generated 50 design variants with CAD models, parts lists and calculations. It assembled a 34-page wiring book in 38 minutes and placed orders for 36 parts from five suppliers totaling $1,933.72. The project consumed a total of 5.7 billion tokens.

title: MIT Han Lab’s Evolving Infra cuts AI agent wait times by up to 14x
summary: A team from MIT Han Lab, with engineers from Georgia Tech, UIUC, UC Berkeley, NVIDIA and OpenAI, has published Evolving Infra, an LLM serving system that adapts to AI agent workloads in real time, mlllm.io reported on November 17, 2026. It separates compute scheduling from KV-cache management, letting nodes switch between prefill and decode modes in seconds, while stale cache is evicted using context-compaction signals from the agents themselves. In tests on up to 256 GB300 GPUs with GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6, it cut average end-to-end latency by up to 4.1x and tail time-to-first-token by up to 14x, and raised throughput by up to 2.7x compared with NVIDIA Dynamo. The code is released under the MIT license, with the Docker image and benchmarks also open.

title: Algeria repays Lawrence, Kansas, for welcoming its World Cup team with a trip of a lifetime
summary: When team Algeria chose Lawrence, Kansas, as its base for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, locals and hundreds of members of the North American Algerian diaspora embraced the team, and now Algeria has returned the kindness, Good News Network reported on November 17, 2026. At the invitation of Algeria’s president, Lawrence Mayor Brad Finkeldei, members of the fan group L’Algerie fi Kansas City, local police officers who provided security for the team and Kansas City residents traveled to Algeria in early November. They landed at 4:30 a.m. to find dozens of government and hospitality representatives waiting with flowers. “We as Lawrence residents didn’t adopt the team,” resident Aaron Downey told the Guardian in June. “I think the Algerians adopted us.” The visitors toured sites including the Roman and Carthaginian ruins at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Tipaza.

title: The West Coast’s first-ever sea turtle hatchlings head out to the Pacific
summary: Olive ridley sea turtle hatchlings saved from an approaching storm in California were released into the wild over the weekend, Good News Network reported on November 17, 2026. In late September, a female turtle dug a nest on a Southern California beach, and a second nest on Huntington Beach a day later marked the first recorded sea turtle nests on the West Coast. When storms were forecast, state and federal authorities moved the eggs to the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach. The hatchlings were measured and then released on Orange County beaches, scurrying down to the water on their own. “Their populations have increased substantially throughout portions of their range,” said Jonathan Snyder of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, crediting decades of conservation work.

title: Collage your own flyers at AcA’s Artist Round Up for the Community Art Zine
summary: The Acadiana Center for the Arts hosts Artist Round Up: Collaging, Flyer Making, and the Community Zine on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, from 6 to 8 p.m. at 101 W. Vermilion St., according to AcA’s event page. Former Artist Alliance member Jesse Poimboeuf leads a night of collaging and mixed-media artmaking as participants put together the 7th issue of the Creative Acadiana Community Art Zine. Inspired by grassroots flyers handmade by the Artist Alliance in the ’90s, attendees will collage flyers of their own for real events, fake events or anything they can imagine. Collaging materials and scissors are provided, and guests are encouraged to bring old photos, stickers or patterned paper. Creatives of all levels are welcome, and the listing asks guests to RSVP.

title: Main Library’s Contemporary Fiction Book Club discusses “Live Fast” tonight
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Contemporary Fiction Book Club meets Wednesday, November 18, 2026, from 6 to 7:30 p.m. at the Main Library, according to the library’s event listing. This month’s discussion is Live Fast by Brigitte Giraud. The in-person meeting is in the Small Conference Room on the second floor. The club is for ages 18 and up.

title: Twenty Years of Valcour Records brings Cajun and Creole stars to the AcA stage
summary: The Acadiana Center for the Arts presents Twenty Years of Valcour Records on Thursday, November 19, 2026, from 7:30 to 9:30 p.m. in the James Devin Moncus Theater at 101 W. Vermilion St., part of its Louisiana Crossroads series, according to AcA’s event page. The concert honors the Eunice label founded by Joel Savoy and Phillip LaFargue, which has preserved Cajun, Creole, zydeco and folk traditions for two decades. Performers include C.J. Chenier, T’Monde, Pine Leaf Boys, The Band Courtbouillon featuring Wayne Toups, Caleb Klauder and Reeb Willms, and Sammy Lind and Nadine Landry. Tickets were listed at $40, but the show has sold out. Fans can join a waitlist or watch the concert online.

title: Trivia Night on the back patio at The Flats downtown
summary: The Flats hosts Trivia Night on Thursday, November 19, 2026, starting at 7 p.m. sharp, according to Downtown Lafayette’s event listing. Players gather on the back patio for four rounds of general knowledge trivia. Teams can have one to six players, and prizes go to the teams with the top three scores of the night. Downtown Lafayette notes that metered street spaces are free after 5 p.m. on weekdays.

title: Accidental Astronauts blasts off at the Science Museum planetarium on Saturday
summary: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette Science Museum shows Accidental Astronauts on Saturday, November 21, 2026, from 11:15 a.m. to noon, according to the museum’s event page. The space adventure for all ages follows Cy, Annie and their dog Armstrong on an unexpected journey into space. Guided by a wise-cracking spaceship computer, viewers explore the Earth, Sun and Moon system, see an asteroid crash into the Moon, bounce along the lunar surface and get up close to a solar storm. The museum also lists The First Stargazers, a 25-minute show about how ancient people experienced the sky, at 1:30 p.m. the same day.

title: Kids can get crafty at Saturday’s Crafternoon at the Main Library
summary: The Lafayette Public Library hosts Crafternoon on Saturday, November 21, 2026, from 2 to 3 p.m. at the Main Library, according to the library’s event listing. “Come get crafty!” the listing says, promising freestyle crafting with all supplies provided. The program is for ages 5 to 12 and takes place in the Craft Room on the first floor. The library’s calendar also lists Makerspace Open Access at the Main Library starting at 9 a.m. that day.
